description.value:
You've learned to wield tech powers pulled from schematics, channeled through your wristpad. Chapter 10 covers the general rules for techcasting, and chapter 12 lists the available tech powers.

Tech Powers Known. You start with 3 tech powers of your choice, learning more as you level per the Tech Powers Known column of the Slicer Pursuit Techcasting table, never exceeding your Max Power Level.

Tech Points. Your tech point pool equals half your scholar level (per the Tech Points column of that table) plus your Intelligence modifier, spent to cast your powers. All spent points return after a short or long rest.

Max Power Level. Many powers can be overcharged by spending extra tech points for a stronger effect, up to a ceiling that rises with level, shown in the Max Power Level column. Casting a power overcharged to 4th level is limited to once, regained after a long rest.

Techcasting Ability. Intelligence governs your tech powers; use it whenever a power calls for your techcasting ability, including for a power's save DC and attack rolls made with it.

Tech save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Tech attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Techcasting Focus. A wristpad (chapter 5 of the Player's Handbook) serves as your tech focus.
